title: Freddie Keppard's style, New York trip and recording
summary: He recalls Keppard's loud outside-man playing, the Coconut Grove job, drinking habits, reading ability and the head arrangements on the record.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: We only have another minute or so on here. I wonder if you have anything to add to what you said about Freddie Kepard. Since he's not here anymore to talk for himself, do you remember about his tone and style? Of course, we can hear it on the record, but a lot of people say he sounded much better than that, even.

But, yes, Freddie Kepard was a great outside man, we would call him. I know that the story of him, Tim Brim in New York, that the Coconut Grove had a band, a great band over there, something like 15 pieces. And he wanted, he kept hearing about this New Orleans style of music. So Freddie Kepard told me. So Freddie showed me the telegram that Tim Brim wanted him to come immediately, to join him at the Coconut Grove in New York. And Freddie was in love with Chicago. And so he went over to New York, and the story is, out that he just went over big in New York at the Coconut Grove. That was a spot for society dancers. They said they never heard such music. And he played what you call on the outside of the band. They would just do an organ or some sort of a beat or riff behind his work, and he could take that derby and do wonders.
Featured by himself with the band behind him. That's all he did.
Would that be for a whole number or just a certain chorus?

Just parts of the numbers. Yeah. And Freddie Kepard, I think, could blow at something louder than any man I ever heard. Do you remember? He could blow above the band. The band would be just blowing what we call a double F, double F-Z. And Freddie Kepard must have been five Zs, because he was above, you could hear him above the band. And he, one peculiarity he had, he weighed about 275 or something, approaching 300. And he liked his fresh refreshments. And that was all in the contract. He would set it down by the pitcher. And he would just sip and blow.
Do you remember if he would read music much, ever use arrangements, or mostly just from his head and by ear?
Yes, Freddie could read music. He could, he could read music.
But generally, generally, he prefer improvising. Yeah.
On the records you made, were any of those things written out, or just all, and you taught them that tune?
Well, just the, just the, what we call head, all from the middle.
